beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Champ, what shape is this?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: A square.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Could it also be a rectangle?

do.text: Could it also be a rectangle?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: No. A rectangle is long.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Let's test that idea using the rules for each name.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Start with a closed, flat shape made of four straight sides. That's a quadrilateral.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Opposite sides do not share a corner. Watch the blue pair, then the purple pair.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Swing the sides until both opposite pairs are parallel.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Parallel lines stay the same distance apart and never meet, even if extended.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A quadrilateral with two pairs of parallel opposite sides is a parallelogram. Add that name. Keep quadrilateral.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Straighten the corners. A right angle is a square corner. Four right angles make this a rectangle.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Does it stop being a parallelogram?

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: No. Both pairs of opposite sides are still parallel.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Shorten the two long sides until all four sides have equal length. The corners stay square.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four equal sides make it a rhombus. Matching tick marks mean equal lengths.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Four equal sides and four right angles together make a square.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Five names for one shape! It kept every earlier rule.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Think of each category as a room with an entry rule. Here is the quadrilateral room.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The parallelogram room fits inside it. Every parallelogram has four sides.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Inside that, rectangles need four right angles. Rhombuses need four equal sides.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: These rooms overlap. Shapes meeting both rules are squares. The overlap is the entire square room.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Squares are a subcategory of rectangles: a smaller group entirely inside a larger group.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: So every square is a rectangle. It already has all four right angles.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Is every rectangle a square? Look at this long rectangle.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: It has four right angles, but its sides aren't all equal. It belongs here, outside the square room.

do.text: This rectangle is not a square.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: One example that breaks a claim is a counterexample. This one proves that not every rectangle is a square.

do.meaning: One example that makes a claim false.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A property is a fact about a shape. Every parallelogram has opposite sides of equal length.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Watch those matching ticks as we make a rectangle. The opposite lengths stay equal.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A rhombus belongs to the parallelogram group too. Its opposite sides are equal, with all four equal.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: And a square belongs to both groups. It inherits the equal opposite sides as well.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Try another. Every rectangle has four right angles. Squares are rectangles. What must every square have?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Four right angles. And because squares are rhombuses, four equal sides too.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: List every name for this marked shape. It has four right angles, and sides of six and three centimeters.

do.text: List every name for this marked shape.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Rectangle, parallelogram, quadrilateral.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Yes. Four right angles, two pairs of parallel sides, and four sides. All three names fit.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Six and three are unequal, so rhombus and square do not fit. Give every name whose rule is met.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Always, sometimes, or never? A rhombus has four equal sides.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Always. That's its rule.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: But equal sides don't force right angles. This rhombus is a counterexample.

do.text: Equal sides do not force square corners.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A rectangle is a rhombus. Always, sometimes, or never?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Sometimes. When all four sides are equal, it's both. It's a square.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: For trapezoids, check the definition. Here we'll use a quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Is this trapezoid a parallelogram?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Never with that rule. A parallelogram needs two pairs.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Some books use at least one pair instead. Always read the definition your question uses.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: When a question asks for several true statements, test each one separately. Every rhombus is a parallelogram.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: True. Both opposite pairs are parallel.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Every rhombus has four right angles.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: False. This rhombus doesn't.

do.text: False: this shape is a counterexample.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Every rhombus with four right angles is a square.

do.text: Every rhombus with 4 right angles is a square.

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: True. Equal sides plus right angles. Keep every true statement, even when several describe the same shape.

do.text: Check every statement on its own.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Triangles sort by rules too. Compare the three side lengths: four, five, six centimeters.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: No two are equal. This is scalene.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Change the four to five. Five, five, six. Exactly two equal sides: isosceles.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: The matching ticks identify equal sides, even when no lengths are written.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Now six, six, six centimeters. What name fits?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Equilateral. All three sides are equal.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Here, isosceles means exactly two equal sides. Three equal sides means equilateral. Use the lengths or matching marks to decide.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: Back to our square. Which names does it wear?

beats.speaker: learner
beats.say: Square. Rectangle. Rhombus. Parallelogram. Quadrilateral.

beats.speaker: teacher
beats.say: A shape belongs to every room around it, and takes every property of those rooms with it.
